newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: "Broker, beware" says S.Africa insurance ombudsman.
newsitem.headline: "Broker, beware" says S.Africa insurance ombudsman.

text.p: South Africa's Life Assurance Ombudsman Jan Steyn on Friday warned the insurance industry that sharp and sometimes dishonest selling practicesby insurance brokers were coming under increasing public and legal scrutiny.

"Broker, beware," he told a media briefing on his latest annual report, which showed that the number of complaints received by his office in the first four months of 1997 totalled 160 a month compared to 117 a month in the same period in 1996.

He said although the industry had, under public pressure, introduced measures to explain policies more clearly to the public and give them a "cooling off" period before they signed up, it was still to early too say if this was enough.
"There are bound to be changes in the emerging markets for life assurance policies, which will put additional pressures on the industry," he said.
To cope with these changes, his office had decided to adjust its charter to play a more active role through conciliation and mediation to resolve disputes.
It had also recommended that an independent panel be established to advise him on particularly tricky cases, such as evaluating disability claims.
